title: Similar String Groups
description:
Two strings `X` and `Y` are considered similar if either they are identical or we can make `X` equal to `Y` by swapping two letters at different positions within `X`.

For example, `"tars"` and `"rats"` are similar (swapping indices `0` and `2`), and `"rats"` and `"arts"` are similar, whereas `"star"` is not similar to `"tars"`, `"rats"`, or `"arts"`. Together, these form two connected groups by similarity: `{"tars", "rats", "arts"}` and `{"star"}`. Notice that `"tars"` and `"arts"` belong to the same group through `"rats"` even though they are not directly similar.

You are given a list `strs` of strings where every string is an anagram of every other string in `strs`. Return the number of similarity groups.
constraints: strs[i] consists of lowercase English letters only.
All words in strs have the same length and are anagrams of each other.
hints: Because every pair of strings in strs is guaranteed to be an anagram, two strings are similar if and only if they differ in 0 or 2 character positions.
Model each string as a vertex in a Disjoint Set Union (DSU) structure and union every pair of similar strings.

Before comparing two strings character-by-character, check if they are already in the same DSU component to skip unnecessary work, and stop scanning as soon as more than 2 mismatched positions are found.

examples.explanation: 'tars' and 'rats' differ at positions 0 and 2, and 'rats' and 'arts' differ at positions 0 and 1, forming one group of 3. 'star' differs from all three in more than 2 positions, forming a second group.
'omv' and 'ovm' differ at positions 1 and 2, so they belong to the same group.
